title: How Significance Built a 900-Line Capability Matrix and Sharper Bid Decisions with GovDash
body_markdown:
## **Overview**


*Significance, Inc. uses GovDash to qualify opportunities, map capabilities to requirements, and build compliant responses as it moves into full-and-open competition.*


Significance, Inc. is a federal professional services and technology consulting firm. The team specializes in digital transformation, financial management, ERP modernization, data analytics, and automation. Its primary customers include the U.S. Marine Corps, Department of the Navy, Department of the Air Force, Space Force, DLA, DFAS, SBA, and DHS.


We sat down with the Significance growth team to discuss how they use GovDash across capture and proposal development.


Significance has about 150 employees and runs a lean growth organization. BD, capture, proposal, pricing, contracts, technical SMEs, and executive leadership all contribute to each pursuit. As the company positions for larger, full-and-open competitions, it needed a capture process that scales with the same team.


### **By the numbers**


- Proposal outlines from **2 days to 3-4 hours**


- **4 RFI responses** per month


- **900-line-item** capability matrix built in GovDash


- **421 contracts** organized in GovDash


## **The challenge**


Before GovDash, moving an opportunity from identification to submission took a lot of manual work. The team read long solicitations by hand, built compliance matrices from scratch, and searched old proposals and corporate materials for relevant past performance.


Qualification started with roughly 100,000 GovWin listings, narrowed to 200-250 potential pursuits and then 40-120 high and medium priorities. Past performance lived in individual team members' files, which made it hard to find the right example when operating against a deadline.


That process took time from the people Significance needs most. Technical SMEs and operational leaders were spending hours on document review instead of supporting customers and shaping solutions. Compressed solicitation timelines made it harder to run bid/no-bid evaluations across several opportunities at once.


Significance set a goal to establish a system to make better pursuit decisions and protect proposal quality while bidding on more complex work.


## **Why GovDash**


Significance found GovDash while evaluating AI platforms built for federal BD, capture, and proposal work. General-purpose AI writing products were ruled out early. The team wanted a platform that understood the federal contracting lifecycle.


GovDash the right fit for three reasons:


- **It covers the full pursuit.** GovDash supports requirement analysis, capability assessment, content organization, and response development in one platform.


- **It runs on Significance's knowledge.** Corporate capabilities, past performance, and technical materials feed directly into opportunity assessments and drafts.


- **It fits Significance’s existing process.** The growth team kept its structure and roles. GovDash slotted into how they already work.


The company also saw a parallel with its own mission. Significance helps federal agencies modernize their operations, and GovDash lets it do the same for its own BD function.


> *"GovDash helps extend our team's capacity, allowing us to pursue opportunities more strategically without proportionally increasing proposal overhead."*


## **From solicitation to compliant draft**


Significance uses GovDash at each step between a new solicitation and a proposal submission.


- **Capture** supports opportunity assessments, competitive positioning, capability alignment, and bid/no-bid decisions.


- **Proposal** builds initial technical narratives and structured responses mapped to solicitation requirements.


- **The Word add-in** strengthens technical language and checks consistency and compliance inside existing drafts.


- **Corporate knowledge and past performance** surface relevant experience and tie it to specific requirements.


Solicitation reviews, capability assessments, compliance analysis, and first-draft narratives used to take extensive manual review and coordination. GovDash now handles that groundwork, so the team moves faster into solution development and proposal refinement.


Proposal outlines that took two days now take three to four hours. The team responds to four RFIs a month and has built a 900-line-item capability matrix in GovDash. Its data library holds 421 contracts, so past performance is searchable and tied to requirements instead of scattered across personal files.


Onboarding followed the same logic. Significance started on live opportunities instead of running a separate technology rollout. Using GovDash on real pursuits showed the team where it added the most value, and those uses became part of its standard workflow.


## **Sharper bid/no-bid calls**


For Significance leadership, the biggest change is in pursuit decisions. Full-and-open procurements are larger and more competitive, so every bid has to be weighed against real capabilities, relevant past performance, competitive position, and ability to execute.


GovDash makes that assessment faster and more consistent. The team can evaluate several opportunities in parallel and bring the same structured view of requirements and capability fit into every bid/no-bid discussion. Leadership uses it to decide whether an opportunity is a realistic path to award or whether resources belong elsewhere.


That keeps growth investment focused on opportunities where Significance has a credible, differentiated position.


> *"Our objective is to pursue the right opportunities with a higher degree of confidence and a stronger understanding of what it will take to win."*


## **Built into the existing stack, with people in charge**


Significance still runs pipelines in Salesforce, writes in Microsoft Word, prices in Excel, and collaborates in SharePoint. GovDash sits alongside those tools and adds requirement analysis, content development, and opportunity evaluation on top.


Human oversight stays in place throughout. Capture managers, technical leads, and proposal professionals validate content, confirm compliance, and make every final strategic call. GovDash does the groundwork; the team makes the judgment calls.


## **Use cases**


- Opportunity qualification and bid/no-bid support


- Capability assessments against solicitation requirements


- Compliance analysis and compliance reviews


- Past performance discovery and mapping


- First-draft technical narratives and structured responses


- Proposal refinement and consistency checks in Word


## **What's next**


Significance plans to expand GovDash across more of its capture lifecycle. Next up are capability gap assessments, past performance mapping, competitive analysis, and proposal quality assurance. The team also wants standardized capture and proposal workflows that hold across customers and procurement types.


Longer term, Significance sees GovDash as the base for a stronger corporate knowledge base, more proposal reuse, and better information for leadership's growth decisions.


## **Advice for other defense contractors**


Significance recommends treating GovDash as a capture and proposal platform and building it into existing BD processes. Their advice: start with real opportunities, set up repeatable workflows, and focus first on the most time-consuming work, such as solicitation reviews, compliance analysis, past performance mapping, and first drafts. Keep strong human oversight in place throughout.


> *"For growing defense contractors, the opportunity is to increase the effectiveness of your existing team while maintaining the discipline and quality required to compete successfully in the federal market."* **Significance, Inc. leadership**
